acceptance: For every platform with a managed deployment mode, a non-interactive run without the acknowledgement exits with the documented code before an adapter is constructed; a test asserts no connection or credential lookup occurred.
With the acknowledgement, the run proceeds exactly as today, and the bundle's execution block records the acknowledgement and its source.
Local and self-hosted runs, and interactive terminal runs, behave as before; tests cover each.

The same rule applies to compare when it runs platforms, and to MCP run_benchmark and start_benchmark. For MCP the acknowledgement comes from how the operator started the server, never from a tool argument the model can set; a test proves a tool argument cannot grant it.

Every in-repository caller that runs a managed platform non-interactively (the UAT matrix in tests/uat/matrix.py, and any workflow) is updated and listed in the PR, and the changelog.d fragment marks the change as breaking.
Help text and user documentation state the rule and its limit: it prevents accidental spend and makes intent visible; it does not stop a caller that sets the acknowledgement itself.
context:
Origin: adversarial review on 2026-11-13 of work first left unfiled. The earlier reasons assumed a person at the keyboard; this item records the corrected disposition. Line numbers are hints; re-read the cited file before relying on them.

Evidence: the confirmation is guarded by 'sys.stdin.isatty() and sys.stdout.isatty() and not s.non_interactive'. A search of the CLI and MCP code found no spend, budget or billable guard on run.

Decision gates (settle in the PR description before coding): (1) the acknowledgement's form. Default: an environment variable plus an equivalent CLI flag, with the environment variable the only form MCP accepts at server start. (2) What counts as billable. Default: deployment mode 'managed' only; list every affected platform, and say whether any self-hosted mode with credentials should be added. (3) The exit code. Follow the table set by compare-exit-codes-distinct-outcomes-20261112 if it has landed; otherwise choose an unused code and record it there. If the resolved deployment mode is not known before adapter construction, stop and report; do not move the check after the connection.

Validator notes. Guaranteed invariant: no non-interactive managed run starts without an acknowledgement in the invocation or environment. False negatives: a caller that sets the acknowledgement itself; a billable service reached through a self-hosted mode. False positives: free-tier managed runs. Maintenance trigger: every new platform or deployment mode.

Verification rubric: pass only if the refusal is proven to precede any connection, the MCP argument test exists, and no live-cloud run was used to test it.

Guardrails: work only in a linked worktree (make worktree-create, then make agent-write-preflight); never edit the primary clone. One PR per item, squash-merged to develop (site work: one PR in BenchBox-dev/benchbox-site). Add a changelog.d fragment for any user-facing change. No live-cloud runs and no credentials in Git or logs. Heavy work (benchmarks, test tiers) runs only through lock-taking entry points or make heavy-run after make heavy-status. Follow the comment policy (make comment-policy-check). Stop and report instead of widening scope; scope removed during review must be re-homed to a named item or dropped by the owner with a reason.
description:
Problem: the only check before benchbox run executes is the 'Proceed with execution?' prompt, and it is shown only when stdin and stdout are terminals and --non-interactive is not set (benchbox/cli/commands/run.py, just before 'Step 6 of 6'). An agent or a CI job therefore reaches a billable managed platform with no check at all. The MCP run tools are non-interactive by nature. This project's own rules bar its agents from live-cloud runs without approval, but the product gives a user's agent no equivalent.

Outcome: in non-interactive mode, a run against a platform whose resolved deployment mode is 'managed' (DeploymentCapability in benchbox/core/platform_registry.py) refuses to start unless an explicit acknowledgement is present. The refusal names the platform and the acknowledgement, happens before any credential read or network connection, and uses a documented exit code. The bundle records that the acknowledgement was given and where it came from.

This is a guard, not an estimator: it predicts no cost and needs no pricing data.

Non-goals: interactive behaviour; local and self-hosted platforms; cost estimation; budget caps.
